no_frame.label: No frame
no_frame.description: Comments that sustain none of the frames: greetings, praise or support without argument, generic insults without a reason, unrelated topics, tags, stickers or missing text.

frames.label: Quality beliefs and false sense of safety
frames.argument: Water from the family mine or well does not need testing because it looks clear, flows continuously and has been consumed for generations without perceived illness.

threads.label: Tradition and experience as guarantee
threads.description: We always drank it and never got ill; spring water that has sustained life for centuries.

threads.label: Bounded autonomous use
threads.description: Own water is used for irrigation, garden, vegetable plot, washing or other non-potable uses, assuming it needs no control.

threads.label: Testing as a condition / right to use
threads.description: Own water is safe (sometimes 'if it is tested periodically') and the right to use or test it without obligation is defended.

threads.label: Ambivalence: risk depends on place
threads.description: Wells may be contaminated and the network is sometimes unfit too; safety depends on the location.

frames.label: Tariff resistance and rejection of centralised management
frames.argument: AdAM bills and charges are seen as disproportionate compared with historical local costs, leading residents to keep or reactivate their own wells to avoid mandatory charges.

threads.label: Fixed charges and zero consumption
threads.description: Paying without consuming, or paying sanitation/waste charges where no service exists.

threads.label: Previous municipal management and non-member municipalities
threads.description: Comparison with municipal management before AdAM or with municipalities that did not join; criticism of handing over the water.

threads.label: Individual exit: own well, mine, spring or disconnection
threads.description: Keeping a private source, trying to disconnect, or rejecting the mandatory connection.

threads.label: Mobilisation and reversal
threads.description: Political mobilisation, demonstrations and demands to reverse the multimunicipal system ('reversao').

threads.label: Price versus service
threads.description: Meter reading left to the customer, estimated bills, customer service, digitalisation, 'water at the price of gold'.

frames.label: Institutional distrust and perceived environmental hypocrisy
frames.argument: Alerts and campaigns from public bodies (advice against drinking from public fountains, calls to save water) are met with scepticism; residents accuse the bodies of ignoring industrial, wastewater-plant or mining discharges into rivers.

threads.label: Official denial versus neighbours' suspicion
threads.description: Foam, sewage or pollution in rivers and beaches: official explanation (natural phenomenon) against local suspicion.

threads.label: AdAM alert read as marketing or monopoly
threads.description: A warning about private water sources is read as a sales pitch, a business or a monopoly move.

threads.label: Closure or neglect of public fountains
threads.description: Fountains were closed or abandoned and are no longer tested or signposted as they used to be.

threads.label: Industrial or extractive contamination and complicity
threads.description: Mining, lithium, kaolin or wastewater-plant pollution and the inaction or complicity of authorities.

threads.label: Hypocrisy of water-saving campaigns
threads.description: Citizens are asked to save while leaks run for days or public lawns are watered.

frames.label: Invisible risks and public-network supply failures
frames.argument: The public supply is not seen as an absolute guarantee of safety, which motivates the search for underground alternatives even without control of nitrates or bacteria.

threads.label: Organoleptic quality of the network
threads.description: Chlorine or bleach smell, turbid, muddy or discoloured water, taste of earth.

threads.label: Pressure, continuity, cuts and pipe breaks
threads.description: Loss of pressure, daily cuts, long outages and unrepaired breaks.

threads.label: Network intake from a polluted river
threads.description: The network water is abstracted from a river with pollution or quality problems.

stance_definitions.supports: The comment sustains or reproduces the argument of the frame/thread.
stance_definitions.opposes: The comment contradicts or rebuts the argument of the thread (e.g. gives a natural explanation for foam, or defends paying waste charges even without consumption).
stance_definitions.qualifies: The comment accepts the argument only partly, adds conditions or doubts.

evidence_definitions.core: The comment reproduces almost literally the target argument of the frame.
evidence_definitions.adjacent: The comment gives evidence for the same frame without stating the whole argument.

decision_rules: F1 requires a reference to the author's own or a private water source (well, mine, spring, borehole, fountain) and to its quality, safety, testing, tradition or use. Rejecting a mandatory connection because of price is F2, not F1.
Attacking the issuer of an alert about private water sources (the concessionaire or the municipality) is F3 (secondary frame F1 if the author also defends their own water).

Tie-break when two frames weigh the same: choose as primary the frame that matches the target of the criticism: price or charges -> F2; the issuing institution or its campaigns -> F3; quality or continuity of the public network -> F4; the author's own water source -> F1.
Leaks, water running in the street or public lawns being watered, mentioned under a water-saving campaign, are F3_H5. The same complaint on a post unrelated to saving campaigns is F4_H2.
Charges for services the author says they do not use, or that do not exist at their address (sanitation, waste), are F2_H1 even when the author also keeps a private source (then secondary frame F1).

Pure agreement, praise or encouragement ('Parabéns', 'Força Sr. Presidente', 'Exatamente', 'Apoiado', emojis) is no-frame. Exception: an endorsement counts as adjacent evidence only if the text itself names the subject, e.g. 'Reversão!!', 'Reversão em todos os municípios', 'espero que a Câmara de Viana tome a mesma atitude' (F2_H4), or a concrete figure or item of the bill (F2_H1).

Generic insults to the concessionaire or to politicians ('ladrões', 'roubo') without a stated reason are no-frame; with a stated reason (a number, a charge, a comparison) they are adjacent evidence for F2.
Customer-service complaints (phone not answered, app not working) are no-frame unless tied to billing, meter reading or price (F2_H5).

Explanations that foam, discolouration or turbidity are natural phenomena (algae, organic matter, wind-blown dust, natural surfactants) are F3_H1 with stance 'opposes'; asking for laboratory samples to document the case is F3_H1 with stance 'qualifies'.
Comparisons with municipalities that did not join the multimunicipal system (e.g. Monção, Melgaço, Ponte da Barca) are F2_H2.

Actor signals: tag micro-level categories when the author says they own or use a well, mine, spring, borehole or public fountain; tag meso or exo categories only when the text states a role (e.g. 'sou presidente da junta'). Post authors are not tagged automatically.

input.text: Bebi sempre da água do poço e das fontes e nunca adoeci. A da rede cheira a cloro.

output.literal_excerpt: Bebi sempre da água do poço e das fontes e nunca adoeci
output.rationale: Years of drinking well and fountain water without illness as a guarantee; contrasts it with the chlorine smell of the network.
output.actor_evidence: Bebi sempre da água do poço

examples.note: Core F1 evidence plus a self-declared private-source user.

input.text: Casa fechada em Neiva, consumo zero e pago mais de 20 euros todos os meses. Isto é roubo.

output.literal_excerpt: consumo zero e pago mais de 20 euros todos os meses
output.rationale: Fixed charge without consumption seen as disproportionate.

examples.note: Firm adjacent evidence: explicit reason and figures.

input.text: Pois, a água vem da ETAR e vai para a ETA... bom proveito.

output.literal_excerpt: a água vem da ETAR e vai para a ETA
output.rationale: Irony: suggests the network water is contaminated by wastewater-plant discharges.

examples.note: Irony is coded by its pragmatic meaning and flagged for review.

input.text: O pó trazido pelo vento para a praia explica a espuma. Não é esgoto.

output.literal_excerpt: O pó trazido pelo vento para a praia explica a espuma. Não é esgoto.
output.rationale: Rebuts the sewage suspicion with a natural explanation.

examples.note: A counter-argument inside a thread is coded with stance 'opposes'.

output.literal_excerpt: é uma treta para vender o produto deles
output.rationale: Reads the alert about private sources as marketing; implicitly defends own water.

examples.note: Attacking the issuer of the alert is F3 with F1 as secondary frame.

output.rationale: Praise without argument about any frame.
Encouragement without content; names neither reversal nor charges.
Demands reversal of the concession in all municipalities.

examples.note: An endorsement that names the subject counts.

output.literal_excerpt: Eu gasto 30 de água e no fim pago 95
output.rationale: Bill far above consumption, with concrete figures.

examples.note: Concrete figures make a firm adjacent case.

output.rationale: General discontent with the company and price, without an explicit reason.

input.text: Ligo para o número e ninguém atende.

output.rationale: Customer-service complaint unrelated to billing, price, quality or network failures.

examples.note: Customer-service complaint without a billing link is no-frame.

output.rationale: Agreement understood only through the parent comment (sanitation charge without service).

examples.note: Bare agreement inherits the parent's frame with confidence 1.
